briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon/evening. We will now begin the climate briefing for July 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of the Global Climate Crisis and its Domestic and International Impacts
sections.content: Today, widespread direct impacts of the intensifying climate crisis have been reported globally and domestically. In France and Spain, large-scale wildfires caused by heatwaves led to the evacuation of approximately 375,000 residents and tourists, while heatwaves and droughts are intensifying across Europe [17, 106, 111, 122, 133, 135]. The Asian region is also suffering significant damage from unprecedented heavy rainfall, floods, and typhoons, with severe casualties and property damage, particularly in Afghanistan where houses have collapsed due to torrential downpours [132]. Domestically, rural areas in Gyeongbuk have been directly hit by heatwaves and pests, and even Daegwallyeong is experiencing normalized heatwaves and tropical nights, indicating the disappearance of four distinct seasons [8, 18, 19, 24, 108, 109]. A grim outlook also suggests that climate change is expected to cause 430,000 deaths annually, 90% of which will occur in impoverished nations [7].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Domestic Efforts for Climate Change Adaptation
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, various proactive adaptation efforts to climate change are actively being pursued domestically. Daegu Grand Park has initiated trial planting of southern tree species in preparation for climate change, thereby accelerating green space development [2, 5, 6, 9, 13, 15]. Anseong City is enhancing agricultural sector resilience by developing superior glutinous corn varieties [4]. Gunsan City, Jeollabuk-do's pilot cultivation of triploid oysters is a positive example confirming the potential for high-value shellfish farming in response to climate change [11, 23]. Namwon City has completed the maintenance of its sewage facilities in preparation for more frequent torrential downpours [20]. Furthermore, aT President Hong Moon-pyo emphasized policy efforts, mentioning the need for agricultural structural reform and the establishment of a dedicated climate change department [25]. Yangcheon-gu is strengthening community-based heatwave responses, such as expanding cooling shelters and smart sunshades [26].

sections.title: 🌱 Challenges in Practicing Carbon Neutrality and Monitoring its Implementation
sections.content: Domestic and international efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals are ongoing, but at the same time, demands for evaluation of their effectiveness and for improvements are growing. The Climate Response Center and Future Forest have agreed to cooperate for carbon neutrality and land restoration [1]. Kia is contributing to carbon neutrality through blue carbon by restoring 50,000 pyeong of Seocheon tidal flats and planting halophytes [30, 31, 38, 64, 65]. Chung-Ang University is conducting research on AI-based carbon-neutral cities [29], and Namseoul University is continuing educational and awareness-raising efforts, including graduating 31 specialized carbon neutrality instructors [35]. Meanwhile, a bill aiming for a 69-80% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2040 is awaiting parliamentary approval in August, and Chairman Cho Jung-sik announced that the amendment to the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality would be processed by the end of August [36, 43, 55, 67, 69]. However, criticisms have emerged that local governments' 'carbon neutrality implementation evaluations' are inadequate, with 90% of 'normal progress' lacking factual basis [32, 48]. Concerns about actual reduction effects have also been raised, as the greenhouse gas reduction achievement rate of local basic governments remains significantly low at 40% compared to their policy implementation rate [39, 70].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Transition: Securing Momentum and Facing Constraints for Goal Achievement
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is a key driver for achieving carbon neutrality, and efforts to expand it are intensifying, particularly within the public sector. Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) has fully launched its public sector K-RE100 renewable energy projects by utilizing idle substation sites [72, 76, 89, 98, 103]. The Public Procurement Service and the Korea Energy Agency signed an MOU to support renewable energy transition and expand green public procurement, stating their intention to lead the renewable energy transition by leveraging the purchasing power of the public procurement market [73, 74, 75, 78, 81, 82, 84, 86, 90, 91, 95, 99]. Korea Southern Power (KOSPO) is also making various attempts to expand renewable energy supply, including supporting public renewable energy consulting services and engaging in solar power development on idle state-owned and public lands with private companies [85, 92]. However, analysis suggests that to achieve the 2030 renewable energy target, the pace of wind power deployment must increase tenfold, and solar power by 3.6 times [77, 105]. KDI also pointed out that grid expansion is progressing slowly compared to the increase in domestic renewable energy generation facilities, making the resolution of grid bottlenecks urgent [80].

sections.title: 📰 Discussion on Corporate Climate Responsibility and Research Ethics
sections.content: Discussions are also continuing regarding the scope of corporate responsibility and research transparency in relation to climate change response. France's TotalEnergies is appealing after losing a climate lawsuit, controversially arguing that its customers' greenhouse gas emissions are not the company's responsibility [16, 124]. This is expected to be an important case in redefining legal and social standards for corporate climate responsibility. Furthermore, several international news outlets have raised concerns that taxpayer funds have been allocated to criticized climate change research, highlighting the need for public attention and oversight regarding the transparency and ethics of climate science research [120, 121, 125, 127, 129].

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we have examined the intensifying domestic and international impacts of the climate crisis and various efforts to address them. Faced with the critical challenges of climate adaptation, carbon neutrality, and renewable energy transition, continuous efforts and oversight will be necessary to achieve tangible results. This concludes today's climate briefing.
